{"arxiv_id":"2310.16818v2","arxiv_url":"http://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16818v2","title":"DreamCraft3D: Hierarchical 3D Generation with Bootstrapped Diffusion
  Prior","authors":["Jingxiang Sun","Bo Zhang","Ruizhi Shao","Lizhen Wang","Wen Liu","Zhenda Xie","Yebin Liu"],"published_date":"2023-10-25T17:50:10Z","journal":"","doi":"","summary":"We present DreamCraft3D, a hierarchical 3D content generation method that
produces high-fidelity and coherent 3D objects. We tackle the problem by
leveraging a 2D reference image to guide the stages of geometry sculpting and
texture boosting. A central focus of this work is to address the consistency
issue that existing works encounter. To sculpt geometries that render
coherently, we perform score distillation sampling via a view-dependent
diffusion model. This 3D prior, alongside several training strategies,
prioritizes the geometry consistency but compromises the texture fidelity. We
further propose Bootstrapped Score Distillation to specifically boost the
texture. We train a personalized diffusion model, Dreambooth, on the augmented
renderings of the scene, imbuing it with 3D knowledge of the scene being
optimized. The score distillation from this 3D-aware diffusion prior provides
view-consistent guidance for the scene. Notably, through an alternating
optimization of the diffusion prior and 3D scene representation, we achieve
mutually reinforcing improvements: the optimized 3D scene aids in training the
scene-specific diffusion model, which offers increasingly view-consistent
guidance for 3D optimization. The optimization is thus bootstrapped and leads
to substantial texture boosting. With tailored 3D priors throughout the
hierarchical generation, DreamCraft3D generates coherent 3D objects with
photorealistic renderings, advancing the state-of-the-art in 3D content
generation. Code available at https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DreamCraft3D.","github_url":"https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DreamCraft3D","main_contributions":"The paper introduces DreamCraft3D, a hierarchical 3D content generation method that leverages a 2D reference image to guide geometry sculpting and texture boosting, addressing the consistency issues in existing 3D generation methods. Key contributions include a view-dependent diffusion model for geometry consistency and a bootstrapped score distillation approach for enhancing texture fidelity through alternating optimization of a personalized diffusion model and the 3D scene representation.","methodology":"DreamCraft3D employs a hierarchical generation pipeline. It starts with a 2D reference image and lifts it to 3D through geometry sculpting and texture boosting stages. Geometry sculpting uses score distillation sampling (SDS) with a view-dependent diffusion model (Zero-1-to-3) and progressive view training. Texture boosting involves fine-tuning a personalized diffusion model (DreamBooth) on augmented renderings of the scene, followed by bootstrapped score distillation (BSD).","experimental_setup":"The method was evaluated on a test benchmark of 300 images, including real pictures and those generated by Stable Diffusion and Deep Floyd. Quantitative comparisons were performed against DreamFusion, Magic3D, ProlificDreamer, Make-it-3D, and Magic123 using metrics like CLIP score, Contextual Distance, PSNR, and LPIPS. A user study was also conducted to assess the perceived quality of the generated 3D models.","limitations":"The approach occasionally incorporates frontal-view geometric details into texture due to depth ambiguity and inaccuracies in the depth prior. The method does not explicitly segregate material and lighting from the 2D reference image.","future_research_directions":"Future research could focus on explicitly separating material and lighting from the 2D reference image to improve the quality and control of 3D content generation."}

{"arxiv_id":"2404.04057v3","arxiv_url":"http://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04057v3","title":"Score identity Distillation: Exponentially Fast Distillation of
  Pretrained Diffusion Models for One-Step Generation","authors":["Mingyuan Zhou","Huangjie Zheng","Zhendong Wang","Mingzhang Yin","Hai Huang"],"published_date":"2024-04-05T12:30:19Z","journal":"","doi":"","summary":"We introduce Score identity Distillation (SiD), an innovative data-free
method that distills the generative capabilities of pretrained diffusion models
into a single-step generator. SiD not only facilitates an exponentially fast
reduction in Fr\'echet inception distance (FID) during distillation but also
approaches or even exceeds the FID performance of the original teacher
diffusion models. By reformulating forward diffusion processes as semi-implicit
distributions, we leverage three score-related identities to create an
innovative loss mechanism. This mechanism achieves rapid FID reduction by
training the generator using its own synthesized images, eliminating the need
for real data or reverse-diffusion-based generation, all accomplished within
significantly shortened generation time. Upon evaluation across four benchmark
datasets, the SiD algorithm demonstrates high iteration efficiency during
distillation and surpasses competing distillation approaches, whether they are
one-step or few-step, data-free, or dependent on training data, in terms of
generation quality. This achievement not only redefines the benchmarks for
efficiency and effectiveness in diffusion distillation but also in the broader
field of diffusion-based generation. The PyTorch implementation is available at
https://github.com/mingyuanzhou/SiD","github_url":"https://github.com/mingyuanzhou/SiD","main_contributions":"The paper introduces Score identity Distillation (SiD), a data-free method to distill the generative capabilities of pretrained diffusion models into a single-step generator. SiD achieves rapid FID reduction and surpasses existing distillation approaches in generation quality across multiple benchmark datasets. It also shows that a single-step generator can outperform the original multi-step diffusion model.","methodology":"SiD reformulates forward diffusion processes as semi-implicit distributions and uses three score-related identities to create a novel loss mechanism. This mechanism trains the generator using its own synthesized images, eliminating the need for real data or reverse diffusion. Model-based score-matching loss, specifically a variant of Fisher divergence, is used, and approximated using the derived identities.","experimental_setup":"The method is evaluated on CIFAR-10 32x32, ImageNet 64x64, FFHQ 64x64, and AFHQv2 64x64 datasets. The VP-EDM checkpoints are used as teacher diffusion models. Image generation quality is measured using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS). Precision and Recall are also considered for ImageNet 64x64.","limitations":"SiD requires managing three networks (pretrained score network, generator score network, and generator) simultaneously, increasing memory demands compared to traditional diffusion model training. It also has increased memory allocation and iteration time compared to Diff-Instruct due to the computation of score gradients.","future_research_directions":"Future research directions include exploring LoRA to reduce the memory footprint of the generator score network and generator, and developing more advanced training strategies such as progressively increasing the batch size, annealing the learning rate, and implementing gradient clipping."}
